Evidence Readings / The system is changing. What has reached people?
Evidence Reading

What can we say about people when rules, institutions and payment infrastructure change after the latest representative survey?

The system is changing. What has reached people?

Yemen’s rules, institutions and payment infrastructure have moved faster than its representative evidence about people. The gap between the two is not an answer to guess; it is the next thing to measure.

Evidence periodGlobal Findex fieldwork November 2022 – January 2023 · point-of-sale (POS) counts March 2025 – June 2026 · institutional records June–August 2026
Last reviewed3 October 2026

What not to conclude

Recent infrastructure, regulatory and programme events are not measures of people’s access, use, service quality or outcomes, and the older Findex observation is not a 2026 population rate.

The latest representative observation of account ownership in Yemen remains 11.9% of adults aged 15 and over in the areas surveyed, from Global Findex fieldwork conducted from 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023.

The financial system around that observation has kept moving. Rules changed, reported payment infrastructure expanded, institutional arrangements evolved and programmes advanced. All of that matters, and none of it, by itself, tells us Yemen’s current population-level inclusion rate.

The newest evidence is not always the evidence closest to the outcome.

The founding assembly of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company in August 2026 is current evidence of institution-building. A June 2026 count of POS terminals is current evidence of reported acceptance infrastructure. Neither is a 2026 population estimate.

Four clocks, four questions

Findex answers a question administrative systems cannot: what share of people in the survey population report owning an account as Findex defines it? Its limits travel with the number. It is a weighted survey, not a census; its frame excludes areas holding about 23% of the population; more than a quarter of its primary sampling units were replaced during fieldwork; it cannot be mapped by governorate; and it is not a 2026 rate.

Rules and institutional records can establish that an instruction was issued, an institution was founded or a governance step occurred. They do not establish effective implementation, customer experience, active use or outcomes.

The infrastructure clock moves fastest. POS terminals reported by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden rose from 561 in March 2025 to 1,651 in June 2026 within its reporting scope. That is meaningful administrative evidence, but it does not tell us how many terminals were routinely working, how many unique merchants or customers used them, how reliable or costly the service was, or whether use was repeated. That the count cannot answer those questions is not a failure; it was not designed to.

Programme baselines and targets are valuable management evidence. But a baseline is not a result, a target is not an achievement, and a programme-defined unit is not national prevalence.

There is no single date called “current”

The better question is not “what is the latest number?” but “latest evidence of what?” Currentness is specific to the question. A newer administrative source can sit beside an older representative survey without contradiction, because they answer different questions.

Whether change has reached people is itself a set of measurement questions: access, active use, quality, protection, persistence and outcomes. These are not automatic stages that follow from one another.

What would change this reading?

A new representative measurement of people that keeps comparability on account ownership and adds:

  • active and repeated digital use;
  • saving and borrowing;
  • the purposes of payments;
  • barriers to opening an account;
  • affordability and reliability;
  • fraud and redress;
  • receipt and use of remittances;
  • gaps by gender and income;
  • geography and displacement, where statistically supportable;
  • persistence after programme participation or a transfer.

Read alongside sharper administrative data on unique users, frequency, reliability, cost and complaints, it would not force survey and administrative data into one number. It would build the bridge between what changed in the system and what changed for people.

Related measurement priorities

Each priority below would supply evidence that this Reading says is missing; the link does not mean the priority would settle the Reading.

Measurement priorityP0 · People
A current people-side inclusion baseline
The Global Findex 2025 edition contains 2024 observations for many economies, but Yemen's latest representative account-ownership observation remains 11.9% of adults aged 15 and over in the areas surveyed, for 2022 (from the Yemen Findex 2021 study fielded in 2022–2023). Major payment-system and reform changes are more recent. The latest published people-level values for receiving domestic remittances, and through which channels, are from 2014; the 2021-wave microdata contain these questions, but weighted estimates have not yet been produced.
Evidence needed: New representative Yemen demand-side survey or equivalent approved microdata with weights and clear coverage, including remittance receipt, channel and frequency.
Decision it would strengthen: A current population measure would allow change since the previous wave to be assessed without projecting reform results onto the population.

Related readings

Evidence periodPoint-of-sale (POS) counts March 2025 – June 2026 · institutional records June–August 2026 · project results framework January 2025
When does a payment reform become financial inclusion?
A rule can be issued, infrastructure can expand, institutions can be created and transactions can appear while evidence on reach, repeated use, service quality, protection and outcomes remains incomplete. The question is how far a reform’s effects can actually be traced.
Evidence periodGlobal Findex fieldwork 2022–2023 · point-of-sale (POS) counts March 2025 – June 2026 · project baseline January 2025, target 2030
When the unit changes, the story changes
People, accounts, subscribers, terminals and transactions all describe parts of Yemen’s financial system. They are not interchangeable measures of financial inclusion, and a target or a trend is only as sound as the unit it keeps.
